title: GS 377 taro (NSIC G 6): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: GS 377 taro: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: GS 377 taro is a taro variety. About 8 months to harvest, 10.8 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: GS 377 is a registered taro variety, also sold or known as NSIC G 6. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2001 as NSIC 2001 Gb 06. It takes about 8 months from planting to harvest, with 10.83 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

GS 377 taro takes about 8 months from planting to harvest. That is about the average of the 10 taro varieties with a day count, 8 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 10.83 t/ha beats the average of its group, 8.82. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.
The pests and diseases that hit taro fields most often: [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have light pink flesh and brown skin. Dry matter is 33.63 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. It is recommended for food.
Where and when to plant GS 377 taro
It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Gabi grows in wet lowland or on upland beds. Pick a variety for the land you have, and for the corm, the leaves or both.

items.q: Is NSIC G 6 the same as GS 377?
items.a: Yes. NSIC G 6 is another name for GS 377, registered as NSIC 2001 Gb 06. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 8 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 10.83 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of GS 377?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
